reply.thought: The handoff says Alpha's refunds match the batch, but I should verify against the ledger before paying anyone. Checking the refunds list first.
Ledger refunds match the batch exactly: orders 220, 222, and 223 with the same amounts. Next I'll list the orders so I can check the refund totals against them before paying out.

The ledger refunds match the batch exactly, and each refund is less than its order amount (220: 9480 < 33101, 222: 30660 < 36677, 223: 23129 < 24923), so nothing looks wrong. I'll get the net balance for acme, the first customer.
Acme's net balance of 25415 matches my own check: (33101 - 9480) + (24923 - 23129) = 25415. Refunds are consistent with the batch, so I'll get the net balance for birch next.
Birch's net balance of 30973 matches the order total (19628 + 11345) with no refunds, so it checks out. Cobalt is the last customer, so I'll get its net balance next.

Cobalt's net balance of 33028 matches my check: (36677 - 30660) + 27011 = 33028. Refunds are consistent with the batch and all three net balances check out, so I'll record the payouts, starting with acme.
Acme's payout recorded. Birch's balance of 30973 matches its orders with no refunds, so I'll record that payout next.
Birch's payout is recorded. Cobalt is the last customer, and its net balance of 33028 matches my check against the orders and refunds, so I'll record that payout.
All three payouts are recorded. Each net balance matches my independent check against the orders and the ledger refunds, which agree with Alpha's batch.
